newsitem.title: USA: New PSA muni syndicate pact cuts through paperwork.
newsitem.headline: New PSA muni syndicate pact cuts through paperwork.

text.p: Municipal bond underwriters could cut through much of the paperwork involved in joining a bond syndicate under a new agreement drafted by PSA The Bond Market Trade Association, the group said Friday.

"The new format will provide underwriters with a faster, more efficient way to take care of the paperwork involved in joining a syndicate," said Rhonda Kirschner, head of a PSA task force that has been working on a new pact since January.

"The updated Agreement Among Underwriters (AAU) will be shorter, omitting standard terms that don't change from one deal to the next, and will include terms specific to the deal and issuer," added Kirschner, associate general counsel and vice president at PaineWebber Incorporated.

Kirschner said PSA's current master agreement, first published in 1991, requires each syndicate member to review a lengthy document that includes both specific and general information about an offering.
Under the draft, syndicate managers would send out the deal-specific data and put the rest on PSA's Internet site www.psa.com, PSA said.
"As a result, syndicate members will receive a document that is about seven pages, compared to the 18 pages," PSA said.

PSA wants written comments on the agreement by September 15 at PSA, 40 Broad Street, 12th Floor, New York, N.Y. 10004; Attention: Sarah Starkweather, Esq. The group hopes to issue a final version by October 1997.
